channel.title: Livable Telluride — Weekly Digest
channel.description: This week's upcoming Gov-Hub meetings and community events across the Telluride region (Town of Telluride, Mountain Village, San Miguel County, the Sheridan Opera House, The Alibi, Wilkinson Library, KOTO, telluride.com, and more).

item.title: 📅 The Week Ahead — Oct 19–25
item.description: The biggest thing on the table this week is San Miguel County's Board of Commissioners taking up four Land Use Code amendments that would add an entirely new Natural Resources article to county code — with separate public hearings on forestry, oil and gas, and geothermal operations. That's the kind of foundational change that sticks around for a generation, and public comment is open. Alongside that, Telluride's school board revisits the mill levy override, the Fire District opens its 2027 budget process, Ouray sets new water and sewer rates on first reading, and the Telluride Medical Center weighs a Two Site Model for how and where it delivers care.

item.title: ⚡ [Meeting] Ouray City Council Regular Meeting — 2026-10-19
item.description:
ouraycity • 2026-10-19
A full agenda for Ouray, which marks its 150th anniversary at this meeting. The consequential items: first readings of two ordinances — one setting 2027 water and sewer rates, and one addressing Light Industrial zoning and EQR (equivalent residential unit) calculations. Council also takes up Resolution No. 23, an intergovernmental agreement with the Ouray County Sheriff for full law-enforcement services — a structural decision about how the city gets policed. Resolution No. 24 covers a water service termination agreement. A perimeter trail easement request and a Responsible Entity Agreement round out the action items. On the discussion side, Waterview Phase II rural homes gets a council direction conversation, with the 2024 housing needs analysis and strategy addendum in the packet. Home Trust of Ouray County presents its quarterly housing services report.
⚡ Why it matters: First readings set 2027 water/sewer rates and reshape Light Industrial zoning rules.

item.description: 🎫 Wilkinson Public Library 📍 Program Room 5:30 PM – 7:00 PM · Can AI make art? Should it? What happens to human artists and human audiences when algorithms influence the way art is conceived and consumed? Join acclaimed songwriter and performer Emily Scott Robinson and novelist and former AI ethics insider Jenny Williams for a deep discussion of the impacts AI is already having on creative practice, labor, and industries, along with impassioned hopes for the future—interspersed with songs and readings from these two artists' body of work (100% human-made). Jenny Williams is the author of House of Liars , a new literary psychological thriller about AI, creativity, and motherhood, as well as the novel The Atlas of Forgotten Places (St. Martin's Press) and the novella A Short Future History of Whales (Spotify Audiobook Selects). …

item.title: ⚡ [Meeting] Board of Directors Meeting — 2026-10-20
item.description:
Telluride Fire Protection District • 2026-10-20
The Telluride Fire Protection District board meets October 20th at 5:30 p.m. at Station 1 on Columbia Ave. Leading the agenda is the first reading of the 2027 budget — the opening move in a process that will play out over the next several weeks. The board will also ratify a pre-build contractor agreement with FCI, likely tied to the ongoing Station 3 update, and will receive a wildfire assignment update along with a September report on PANO camera usage. On a brighter note, the district is set to recognize an EMS Excellence in Quality Care and Data Reporting award from CDPHE. Staff reports from the Deputy Chief, Battalion Chief, Fire Marshal, EMS Coordinator, HR Coordinator, and District Chief round out the evening. No executive session is scheduled.
⚡ Why it matters: First reading of Fire District's 2027 budget opens the public funding process.

item.title: ⚡ [Meeting] Telluride Board of Education Monthly Meeting — 2026-10-20
item.description:
Telluride School District • 2026-10-20
The October 20 meeting has a full plate. On the action side, the board votes to approve the Unified Improvement Plan and a resolution recognizing Principal Appreciation Month. Discussion items carry more weight: the MLO and funding update returns — the mill levy override has been a recurring thread through recent meetings, and board members have been doing their own outreach to voters. There's also a housing update, which connects to the district's ongoing effort to build rental and for-sale units at Two Rivers using remaining bond funds — 14 rental and 6 for-sale units were the figures on the table last month. The Unified Improvement Plan gets both discussion time and a formal vote. The board will also work through the student representative process and timeline, CASB planning follow-up, and a TES/TIS school report focused on the ELG Grant. Routine consent items include the September 30 quarterly financials and personnel report.
⚡ Why it matters: Board discusses mill levy override funding — ongoing decision with direct school budget impact.

item.description:
Town of Telluride • 2026-10-21
The two Shandoka Lot Redevelopment hearings (Buildings 1 and 2, and Buildings 3 and 4 on the Town-owned lot at 860 Black Bear Rd) are continued again, without discussion, to the November 18 HARC meeting, and the 448 Tomboy Road application is continued to December 16 at the applicant's request. What HARC actually hears: a request to recommend administrative approval of payment-in-lieu of parking for one space at 510 W Columbia Ave/129 N Townsend in the Historic Residential zone, and small-scale new construction on a steep lot at 785 Primrose Lane. The applicant for the 214 S Fir Certificate of Appropriateness amendment has asked to table it for eight months.

item.title: ⚡ [Meeting] Parks & Recreation Commission - Oct 21 2026 — 2026-10-21
item.description:
Town of Telluride • 2026-10-21
Two substantive action items headline this meeting. First, SBG Productions is asking to restore the Telluride Jazz Festival to a full three-day run — August 13–15, 2027 — after the 2026 event was trimmed to two days in an attempt to cut costs and boost ticket sales; that experiment didn't move the needle, and the 50th anniversary year is the occasion for returning to the traditional format. Commission approval here is a prerequisite before CCAASE takes it up on November 4, followed by Town Council. If fully approved, the festival could draw up to 6,000 people per day, with the Town collecting admissions fees of $4.15 per ticket sold — up to $63,495 for the three-day run. Second, the Commission considers a design concept for expanding the basketball court in Town Park at its existing location. The work session covers seasonal check-ins with the Telluride Soccer Club and Telluride Lacrosse Club. Staff will also brief the Commission on the 2026 project update, 2027 budget, and the upcoming winter season.
⚡ Why it matters: Vote on restoring Jazz Festival to three days affects town events planning and impact.

item.title: ⚡ [Meeting] Board of County Commissioners Meeting — 2026-10-21
item.description:
San Miguel County • 2026-10-21
The headline work here is a suite of four Land Use Code amendments that would add an entirely new Article 6 — Natural Resources — to San Miguel County's code. Three sections get individual public hearings: forestry practices (Section 6-4), oil and gas operations (Section 6-5), and deep geothermal operations (also called Section 6-4 in the agenda, likely a numbering error to watch). A fourth resolution then amends Articles 1, 3, 4, and 5 to align existing code with the new natural-resources framework. That's a significant rewrite of how the county regulates extraction and land management. On the consent agenda: a 2027 Gondola IGA supplement and the Lawson Hill Connector Trail construction agreement. Afternoon items include a possible co-sponsorship of a CDBG grant application to restore water supply to Telluride Pines HOA residents, the 2027 Community Support Funding allocation, a $12,000 food bank request from West End Family Link, and a Public Health strategic plan presentation.
⚡ Why it matters: Public hearings on new county code governing forestry, oil, gas, and geothermal.

item.title: ⚡ [Meeting] Regular Board Meeting — 2026-10-22
item.description:
Telluride Medical Center • 2026-10-22
The Telluride Hospital District board meets October 22 at the Wellness Annex (and via Zoom) for a session that's heavier than usual on strategic decisions. The two items worth watching: a discussion and possible action on a Two Site Model — what that means for where and how THD delivers care is the kind of question that has long-term consequences for the whole region — and a Letter of Intent with CommonSpirit Health, a major Catholic health system, which could shape the district's clinical and financial future considerably. New facility updates and partnership reports round out the facility-planning conversation. On the finance side, the board reviews September draft financials, a mill levy budget discussion, and updates on benefits and grants.
⚡ Why it matters: Possible action on Two Site Model could reshape how and where medical care is delivered.
